Return: the exits are li v0,-1 (0x41a548) and addu v0,a2,t0 (0x41a524/0x41a544; a2 = int loop counter, t0 = lhu 6(client)), unnarrowed, so the return is not a byte or halfword type; the caller does move s5,v0 at 0x41fb04 and then bltz s5,0x41fb60 at 0x41fb08 (signed test of a value that is -1), uses it as addu v1,s5,NetObjectStatus (0x41fb68), sll v1,s5,2 (0x41fb84) and addiu a0,s5,1 (0x41fb94) with 32-bit ops, so it is a signed 32-bit int (a uchar/bool return is zero-extended and could never be negative; a uint would not be tested bltz). recon facts shows only the move because it does not follow s5 (tool gap). Fix: replace the unresolved row with prototype return int, no parameters, evidence as above; re-run recon validate, recon program, preflight-batch (then 1 prototype, 31 unresolved). The other 31 unresolved rows hold: constant-only or 0/1 status returns, untyped records or function-pointer types, address-taken callbacks; recon void verdicts quoted in the plan match; recon draft --check ok.

TWO FINDINGS. (1) 0x199610 CAiMaps::GetLocationDelta returns int without positive evidence. Every exit value is unsigned-typed: sltu-based abs diff of 13-bit uint fields (0x199664/0x1997cc) plus addu (0x1996a8, 0x199810), or lw v0,0(v0) at 0x199830 of ai::_max<unsigned int> (const uint& result). The caller slti at,fp,2 (0x265bf8) after move fp,v0 (0x26507c) only shows the caller's own local is int; a uint return converted to an int local compiles identically, so it is not evidence for the callee's return type, and the 'no narrowing' argument is the inference the Return width rule forbids. Fix: either uint (the returned value's own type, as accepted for GetAwareCounter) or unresolved on signedness, recording width 32 proven. (2) 0x1b47b0 CZAnimBlendMode::GetBlendMode returns int from constants only (li 0/1/2 at 0x1b47f4,0x1b4828,0x1b485c-0x1b4908). The callers' sw v0,0(s4/s3/s2/s1) into int* out-parameters is an unnarrowed use, which the rule says proves nothing about width (a uchar return stores identically); constant-only returns stay unresolved on width, as the planner already did for LeadTargetG, GetRandomLoc, CenterRegion. No DWARF, no member type, no andi. Fix: unresolved (return width unproven; proven parts: static, a0 = _zrdr*, constants 0/1/2). Tool gap: recon void v7 stays open for PrintPath/HandleMoving-style chains through a vtable slot whose base (CSealCtrl::Dump 0x2694f0, void in accepted group 0c23b08b) is already typed void.

No declaration or DWARF exists. Fix: make both rows unresolved with the reason 'return width mixed: callers narrow with andi 0xff (uchar evidence) but the body returns sign-extended -1 and an un-narrowed counter (int evidence); no declaration', keeping the proven parts (static, no parameters, a0 not read). Everything else in the plan checked out: validate, program identity, preflight skips, draft --check, the void rows 0x1f3fb0 (chain closes at RemoteGameUpdateCallback PFiii_v and RemoteGameCreationCallback PFii_v, a3/a2 of zNetRegisterRemoteObjectCallback at 0x206964/0x206960) and 0x2041c0 (a1 of zNetJoin, first PFii_v, at 0x201860/0x203cf4), so a resubmission needs only these two rows changed. Note for the planner: the 0x1f3fb0 evidence omits that RemoteGameUpdateCallback is also called directly from RemoteGameCreationCallback (0x2062f0, returns it), which is itself address-taken as PFii_v; the conclusion stands.

review_history.reason:
4 findings (plan sha256:c97f1200f5f7662654075b0e6a41e30990913c6a0463c89c7428891ecb1ac896; validate, draft --check, program equality and preflight-batch all pass):
(1) 0x418330 NetCreateClient, (2) 0x4183e0 NetFreeClient, (3) 0x4191e0 NetGetClientIpAddress: 'connection' typed uint only from an sltiu bound with no signed test (sltiu at 0x41836c / 0x418404 / 0x419200). sltiu is not positive sign evidence for the declared type: the compiler emits it for signed operands too (MW MIPS C: sltiu at,a1,8 at 0x3d10a4 on the DWARF int index of CWeaponSel::SetItemPos; a folded 'c < 0 || c >= 4' gives the same instruction), and no accepted row has typed uint from sltiu without a mangled Ui or a declaration (NetGetClient and NetGetObject list it only as a proven part). Where the connection value can be observed it is signed: NetJoin stores its a0 into JoinConnectionIndex (sw s4 at 0x41c26c, delay slot of jal NetCreateClient, a0 = that value), and NetFreeRemoteObject compares JoinConnectionIndex signed (slti v0,v0,4 at 0x41a284) before passing it as NetGetClient's connection (move a1,v0 at 0x41a280). The live signatures are Ghidra's default, so every parameter needs a proven type. Fix: leave these three rows unresolved (connection signedness unproven), keeping client int and buffer char * as proven parts, unless positive evidence decides connection.
(4) 0x411280 setNewSeed_platform: 'int seed' is not proven, and the caller's argument setup contradicts it. The only caller zero-extends the argument (dsll32 a0,a0,0 at 0x411268; dsrl32 a0,a0,0 at 0x411270, the delay slot of jal 0x41126c). That conversion is needed for an unsigned or 64-bit parameter, not for an int. The callee's dsll32/dsra32 at 0x411288-0x41128c is the same conversion it applies to the 32-bit lw results before each sw into the seed array (0x4112a8-0x4112b4, 0x4112c0-0x4112cc, 0x4112d8-0x4112e4, 0x4112f0-0x4112fc). So it is a conversion to the array element type, not proof of the parameter's width. The module's int parameters get no entry extension (NetCreateClient client: move s0,a1; bltz s0 at 0x41834c). Fix: leave unresolved (parameter width/signedness unproven: uint or a 64-bit unsigned type), recording void (recon void VERDICT void) as proven.
Not findings: TRC_PowerOffThread void (void * arg) is valid. ThreadParam.entry's DWARF type (DIE 0xe9290 member at +4 -> 0xea999 = void (void *)) is a declaration in the program for the function stored there (store sw v0,52(sp) into the ThreadParam at sp+48 passed to CreateThread; the stores at +8/+12/+16/+20 match the layout). It follows the accepted, applied precedent _Cdvd_cbLoop (group 2f4d708d) and the rules-v11 callback contract. Partial rows rt_time_get_time_string, rt_msg_client_iudp_clear_target (char * address, ushort port from entry andi 0xffff, also masked by its caller and callee), NetFreeRemoteObject (int: slt at 0x41a2ac/0x41a2c0, no entry narrowing), FindFreeDataStreamBlock (int: subu+blez, slt), every 'client int' and NetInitializeClients void (void) are correct.

review_history.reason: (1) 0x1caa50 CZAnim::AddName: the partial row's return is provable, and the plan is inconsistent with its own AddValve row. The body is identical to AddValve (0x1ca9f0): it returns CZAnimNameIndexTable::AddName's accepted int unchanged (jal 0x1caa88; no write to v0 before jr ra at 0x1caa9c). Metrowerks narrows byte returns in the callee: get_valve 0x26baf4 returns an int counter (slti v0,s0,4) with andi v0,s0,0xff in the delay slot of its exit branch, and the same-class 84-byte uchar wrappers CZAnim::SequenceRunning (andi at 0x1cd5f4) and SequenceExists (andi at 0x1cd654) narrow the result they pass through. A uchar AddName would therefore narrow too. The claim that callers narrow comes only from the first 12 listed sites. With --callers 51, callers also store halfwords (sh v0 at 0x1b7060, 0x1b72d0, 0x1c411c, 0x1c41c4), so sb/andi only narrow into byte destinations. Fix: complete row int (CZAnim * this, char * param_2), with the same evidence as AddValve. (2) 0x1c9b90 CZAnim::LoadNodeNames: same finding. Its exits return the int counter a2 (addiu a2,a2,1 with no narrowing; move v0,a2 at 0x1c9cb8, 0x1c9ce8), AddNewNodeRef's result, or s5 (the int param_4 or the counter, move v0,s5 at 0x1c9ee0), all unnarrowed. Callers store the result as words (sw v0,36(s0) at 0x2ba570; sw v0,28(s0) at 0x2bd954; sw v0,172(sp) at 0x1abd6c, then pass it back as the int param_4, lw a3,172(sp) at 0x1ac030 and 0x1ac1e0), as halfwords (sh at 0x1b06c0, 0x1b0784, 0x1b1ab0, 0x1b34c4; andi s1,v0,0xffff at 0x1d050c), and as an index (sll a0,v0,3 at 0x1c9958). Fix: complete row int, citing these sites; the parameters stand. (3) The AddValve int row (0x1ca9f0) stands. Its width comes from the unnarrowed pass-through, and its sign from the callee's accepted int (that row: slt against the int m_count; returns m_count-1), not from the word stores. Cite that, not the stores. All other open rows check out: types unique with exact case, partial-row parameter proofs, zAnim tick/parser contracts, UICommandTable uchar handlers (dispatcher andi at 0x1d027c, 0x1d02cc), CMenuStack missing.

Plan sha256:3a508f38...6d779376 matches; recon validate ok; recon program equals build/apply (sha256:765ec511...); preflight-batch ok, 12 skips = the 12 keep rows; live_signature of all 24 withdraw rows equals recon live. 24 withdrawals and 6 keeps are sound: abs 0x3def20 (its own bgez on the a0 it returns, and callers pass int-int subu), setlocale 0x3e1b08 (_setlocale_r returns the string "C" at 0x466e70 or null), and memchr/memcpy/memmove/memset 0x3e2958/0x3e2ad0/0x3e2b80/0x3e2c88. Judgement (a) is consistent: these four return a pointer their own body dereferences at mixed widths (lq/sq/sd/lbu/sb), so void * claims only a data pointer. The withdrawn char * rows claim a char pointee that nothing proves. Precedent 024: sceDmaPutStallAddr's void * was withdrawn because that body never dereferences the value. No withdrawn pointer result is stored unchanged into a DWARF pointer member. Findings (the fix for each: replace the keep row with a withdraws_return partial row with the live parameters):
(1) 0x3e48f0 rand: the body proves only a 31-bit masked word (and v0,v1,0x7fffffff at 0x3e4914), which fits int and uint. The sign comes only from callers' cvt.s.w and div (0x17e21c, 0x175500). That is consumer use; the user's 2026-10-30 consumer rule covers only a store into a DWARF-typed pointer member.
(2) 0x3e38b0 _ulp: the body builds a 64-bit word with integer ops only (dsll32/sllv/or; move v0,a1 at 0x3e393c), so only the width is proven. double rests on callers passing v0 unchanged to the double parameters of dpadd/dpsub/dpmul (0x3e6ee0, 0x3e7008, 0x3e7158, 0x3e7250). That is a consumer's parameter type, which proves nothing about the producer (PLANNER.md).
(3) 0x3e0540 __errno: the only exit returns the unchanged value of DWARF global _impure_ptr (DIE 0x4f5, a pointer to _reent 0x97d3). The value's own type is therefore _reent *. Reading it as &_errno at +0 (int *) needs the recalled errno.h declaration. The 4 callers' sw v1,0(v0) store through the result (consumer use, not a store of v0 into a member).
(4) 0x3e36b8 __mcmp: subu of two words proves a 32-bit width only, and the -1/1/0 constants fit either sign. int rests on (i) the callers' bltz/bgez/bgtz (consumer use) and (ii) _wds being DWARF int, which holds only if the live _Bigint * parameters do. Those parameters come only from the recalled mprec.h: callers quorem/_dtoa_r/__mdiff/_strtod_r have no DWARF. Repair 026 withdrew sceSifRemoveRpc 0x15e940 on the same ground.
(5) 0x3e7900 strtol and 0x3e7b58 strtoul: the 64-bit width is proven (daddu accumulator after __muldi3), but the sign is not. _strtol_r 0x3e76c8 and _strtoul_r 0x3e7938 use the same sign-neutral ops: the sltu cutoff compare (0x3e7810, 0x3e7a78), __umoddi3/__udivdi3 for the cutoff in both, and dsubu negation under the '-' flag in both (0x3e7884, 0x3e7b04). They differ only in the clamp constants: 0x7fff../0x8000.. versus all-ones, and those constants fit both longlong and ulonglong. Nothing in either body applies a signed compare, signed divide or extension to the value (PLANNER.md integer sign evidence).
Under these rules, a saturation-limit rule or an errno-pointer rule would need a coordinator decision.
